record.text_content: But it will be built in the name of the Lord. Give heed, that the temple of the Lord may be built gloriously. How? Learn: by receiving the forgiveness of sins and hoping in the Name, we became new, created again from the beginning; therefore God truly dwells in us, in the dwelling place of our heart. How? The word of his faith, the calling of his promise, the wisdom of his righteous ordinances, the commandments of his teaching—he himself prophesying within us, he himself dwelling in us—he opens the door of the temple (that is, the mouth) to us, giving us repentance, and thus leads us who had been enslaved to death into the incorruptible temple. For he who desires to be saved looks not to the man, but to him who dwells and speaks in him, and is amazed at him, because he has never either heard such words from the mouth of the speaker, nor has he himself ever desired to hear them. This is a spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

record.text_content: The ninth parable describes those from the eleventh mountain who submitted branches green and with fruit. Two-thirds of their branch was dry and only one-third remained green. These are believers who acquired faith but then became wealthy and distinguished in the eyes of the Gentile world; they clothed themselves in great arrogance and became haughty, abandoning the truth of the faith and detaching themselves from the community of the righteous. They lived alongside the pagans and found that way of life more pleasing. They did not completely abandon God, but they ceased to work the works of faith. Many of them repented and their dwelling was established in the tower. Others persisted in living with the pagans until the end and were entirely consumed by pagan vanities; these were reckoned among the pagans rather than the faithful. A third group fell into double-mindedness, no longer hoping for salvation because of their deeds; some created schisms.
